# Lifecycle Consistency Checklist: Accurate Blocked Session Status

**Purpose**: Provide a formal implementation-approval review of lifecycle accuracy and cross-surface consistency in the feature requirements
**Created**: 2026-10-13
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are all supported primary lifecycle classifications and their mutually exclusive meanings explicitly defined? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Are requirements documented for ordinary operator blocks, recoverable quota waits, and quota failures requiring operator action? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003–FR-005]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the diagnostic fields required for each paused classification completely specified, including the behavior when optional context is unavailable? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003–FR-005, Gap]
- [ ] CHK004 Are removal requirements defined for resume, retry, cancellation, terminal transition, eligibility loss, and cleanup? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK005 Are restart reconstruction requirements bounded clearly between durable quota waits and ordinary non-quota blocks? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, Spec §Out of Scope]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is the precedence rule for overlapping blocked, quota-waiting, retrying, and running records stated unambiguously in the normative feature artifacts? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, Contract §Classification]
- [ ] CHK007 Is “concise, non-secret reason” constrained sufficiently to guide objective acceptance, including normalization and length bounds? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-012, Contract §Safety]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the boundary between an automatically recoverable quota wait and an operator-blocked quota condition objectively decidable from the requirements? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004–FR-005]
- [ ] CHK009 Is “next completed snapshot” defined consistently enough to measure stale-state removal across lifecycle transitions? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, Spec §SC-003]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK010 Do the specification, data model, and projection contract use the same primary lifecycle terms and precedence? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, Contract §Classification]
- [ ] CHK011 Are count, list, and issue-detail requirements consistent in treating one normalized entry as the sole primary representation of an issue? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-008, Contract §Surface behavior]
- [ ] CHK012 Are tracker workflow state requirements consistently supplementary across terminal, JSON, and LiveView surfaces? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006–FR-007]
- [ ] CHK013 Are quota-derived operator blocks consistently required to retain diagnostic quota context while being excluded from quota-waiting counts and lists? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, Contract §Blocked contract]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK014 Can unique classification and count/list equality be measured for every constructed snapshot without relying on implementation-specific knowledge? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–SC-002]
- [ ] CHK015 Do acceptance criteria identify the observable evidence needed to compare lifecycle classification and diagnostic context across all three status surfaces? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK016 Are regression expectations for running, retrying, token, rate-limit, and unavailable states specific enough to detect changed operator meaning? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-013, Spec §SC-005]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements defined for every transition into, within, out of, and across paused lifecycle states? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 3, Spec §FR-009–FR-010]
- [ ] CHK018 Are concurrent or stale-record overlap scenarios addressed without permitting duplicate counts or conflicting primary states? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK019 Are missing session, event, tracker-state, renewal-time, and native-continuation values addressed with deterministic fallback requirements? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases, Gap]
- [ ] CHK020 Is whole-snapshot unavailability clearly distinguished from an issue-level blocked state in requirements and acceptance criteria? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK021 Are live-update requirements explicit that count, row, status, and reason originate from one coherent snapshot? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011, Spec §User Story 3]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK022 Are privacy and display-safety exclusions complete for credentials, prompts, provider payloads, control characters, excess whitespace, and unnecessarily verbose output? [Security, Spec §FR-012, Contract §Safety]
- [ ] CHK023 Is the expected linear classification scale and supported runtime-record volume documented consistently enough to constrain performance validation? [Performance, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK024 Are observability terms and diagnostic fields aligned with the project logging contract without requiring secret or raw payload exposure? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004–FR-005, Constitution §VI]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK025 Are assumptions about the orchestrator as sole mutable-state owner and the projection as a read-only boundary documented consistently? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, Plan §Summary]
- [ ] CHK026 Are dependencies on existing snapshot, PubSub, retry, quota persistence, and unavailable-state behavior identified together with their compatibility constraints? [Dependency, Spec §FR-010–FR-013]
- [ ] CHK027 Are exclusions for new persistence, operator commands, missing-session reconstruction, and unrelated dashboard redesign explicit enough to prevent scope expansion? [Scope, Spec §Out of Scope]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
